narrationScript: Welcome to Cohortia's module on Searching Algorithms. In earlier lessons, we learned that efficient algorithms are crucial as data grows. We explored linear search, a straightforward method, but it has a significant drawback: its worst-case time complexity is O(n). This means for a list of a million items, you might need a million checks. This is simply too slow for many real-world applications. To address this, we'll dive into much faster techniques. By the end of this module, you'll understand why linear search falls short and how to use the powerful Binary Search algorithm. You'll learn to implement Binary Search in C, both iteratively and recursively, and analyze its efficiency using Big O notation. Finally, we'll introduce hashing, a technique offering even faster average-case search times.
